examples.title: getXComponentSurfaceId9+
examples.description:
getXComponentSurfaceId(): string
Obtains the ID of the surface held by the XComponent. This API works only when type of the XComponent is SURFACE ("surface") or TEXTURE.
Atomic service API: This API can be used in atomic services since API version 12.
System capability: SystemCapability.ArkUI.ArkUI.Full
Return value
When you create an XComponent using a custom component node, the onLoad callback is triggered before the onSurfaceCreated callback. This means that calling getXComponentSurfaceId in the onLoad callback will not return a valid surfaceId. You are advised to obtain the surfaceId in the onSurfaceCreated callback instead.

examples.title: Example 1: Enabling AI Image Analyzer
examples.description:
This example shows how to use the enableAnalyzer attribute to enable the AI image analyzer. You can use XComponentController to start or stop AI analysis on images.
For details about how to implement the drawing logic (functions related to nativeRender), see ArkTS XComponent Example.

examples.title: Example 2: Locking the Surface Orientation During Screen Rotation
examples.description:
This example shows how to use setXComponentSurfaceRotation to lock the surface orientation during screen rotation so that the surface does not rotate with the screen.
For details about how to implement the drawing logic (functions related to nativeRender), see ArkTS XComponent Example.

examples.title: Example 3: Drawing Content on the XComponent Using a Canvas Object
examples.description: From API version 20, this example demonstrates how to return a canvas object by calling lockCanvas, call the corresponding drawing API via the canvas object, and then call unlockCanvasAndPost to draw content on the XComponent.

examples.title: Example 4: Implementing an Immersive Effect
examples.description: From API version 20, building upon Example 3, the setXComponentSurfaceRect API is called to set the surface area to achieve an immersive effect.

examples.title: Example 5 Setting Whether the Surface Held by XComponent Needs to Be Treated as Opaque During Rendering
examples.description:
In API version 22 and later versions, this example calls the setXComponentSurfaceConfig API to set whether the surface held by the XComponent is treated as opaque during rendering.
For details about how to implement the drawing logic (functions related to nativeRender), see ArkTS XComponent Example.
